description: Each task maps source page(s) to an expected extraction result. Run your scraper on the sources, write JSON matching the schema, then score it with evaluate.py. Lists are compared order-insensitively; floats with tolerance.

data-attributes.schema: [{sku, name, price: float, currency, in_stock: bool}]

product-cards.schema: [{sku, name, category, price: float (current price), original_price: float|null, rating: float|null, review_count: int|null, in_stock: bool}]

comment-thread.schema: [{id, author, depth: int (0 = top-level), upvotes: int, body}]

quotes.schema: [{text (exact .text span content incl. curly quotes), author, tags: [string]}] — crawl via the Next link

books.schema: [{title (FULL title from the link's title attribute), price_gbp: float, rating: int (from class name), in_stock: bool}]

book-details.schema: [{title, upc, available: int (count inside parentheses), tax_gbp: float}]

countries.schema: [{name (without flag emoji), capital, population: int, area_km2: float}]

corpus-malformed.schema: [{id (data-id), title, price: float, mileage_km: int}] — parser must survive unclosed/mis-nested tags

corpus-legacy.schema: [{name, department, extension}] — data table is nested inside layout tables

corpus-no-semantics.schema: [{title, company, location, salary_min: int, salary_max: int, posted (ISO date)}] — no classes or ids available

feed.schema: [{title, link, pub_date (ISO 8601 with offset)}] — XML, not HTML
